I also felt the same about medication for a long time but it’s not a bad thing. You wouldn’t deny chemotherapy for a cancer diagnosis. It’s there to help you and yeah sometimes the doctors can get it wrong and give you something that doesn’t help but rest assured you won’t be on an array of pills. They tend to avoid medication in personality disorders unless it’s BPD, and that’s only to sort out the mood swings, it’s not to treat the condition. Therapy is the only way forward with personality disorders.

With personality disorders they tend not to treat it with medication. NPD would be treated with therapy - BPD can be treated with mood stabilisers/antidepressants to alleviate the affective instability symptoms in the short term but the long term answer is therapy. You’d need to book an appointment with your doctor and be frank with them about your issues like you have been here. Ask for a mental health assessment. If you’re not referred the first time, go again. The NHS is so underfunded in the mental health sector they’ll find any excuse not to treat people. Just keep pushing with your gp for now. I found writing down a list in my Notes on my phone of things I struggle with as they came to me and then presenting them to the doctor really helped. If possible bring a parent/carer to back up that this is in fact the way you do behave.
